summary: Granite County, MT lookout built about 1938-39 per Forest Lookouts (firelookout.com says 1933); its top cab was moved to the Missoula Smokejumper Visitor Center as a display in 1978, and current display is not confirmed.

facts.design: 50-foot cable-braced round timber tower (plan L-11) with a 14-foot-square L-4 cab
facts.agency: Deerlodge National Forest (original tower); US Forest Service (visitor center display)
facts.status_note: The top cab was moved to the visitor center as a display (planned 1977, moved 1978 per firelookout.com); current display not confirmed. The FFLA lists the original Blackpine Mountain site as gone.

access.note: The Forest Service page says the visitor center is closed for renovations; pre-scheduled tours can be requested by email or phone

events.note: CCC road work under way in July 1938 and being finished in November 1938; plan L-11 tower with L-4 cab completed by the end of 1938 or early 1939, per the Forest Lookouts page; six miles of road reported constructed in the October 1939 item
October 1939 newspaper item, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, reports a 50-foot tower erected
Disputed: firelookout.com says constructed in 1933; not matched by the 1938-39 records
October 1977 newspaper report: the lookout was being disassembled to move to Missoula for display
Cab moved to the Missoula Smokejumper Visitor Center as a display, per firelookout.com

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says 1933; the Forest Lookouts page quotes 1938 road and tower work and an October 1939 erection item. The story uses 1938-39 and marks 1933 as disputed.
The 1977 newspaper report says the cab will be moved; firelookout.com dates the move to 1978. The story gives both.
Firelookout.com gives 7937 feet; the 1939 item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page gives 7,500 feet. Not used in the story.

notes_for_editor: The build date is disputed (1933 against 1938-39), and so is the elevation (7937 ft against 7,500 ft). The 1977 move was planned; firelookout.com dates the move to 1978. The visitor center page says it is closed for renovations; that may have changed by the time anyone visits. We did not confirm that the cab is still on display. Searches: 2 WebSearch calls; about 4 distinct pages read.
